title: Business Development Senior Director at Server Infrastructure Vendor Expects Memory Demand to Grow 20%–30% Amid Tight Supply Through 2027
expert: Business development senior director, North American AI server OEM (system-level view; SK hynix ~30%–40% of memory content)
verdict: Large-volume DRAM lead times stretched to up to 20 weeks from 14–16 last quarter and allocation tightened, while Q3 DRAM prices ran about 30% above last year: supply, not demand, is the binding constraint.

Supply: 🟢 DRAM lead times up to 20 weeks vs 14–16 weeks, last quarter; allocation slightly tighter on HBM and high-capacity DDR5; first read on lead times (no earlier call or stored row). → Supply pillar ↑
🟢 New capacity not meaningful until late 2027 into 2028, consistent with TrendForce (SB #63891).
Pricing: 🟢 Q3 DRAM prices about 30% higher y/y, NAND 10%–20%, first-hand y/y; SK hynix reported 3Q26 DRAM ASP +29% q/q (SB #67578), so the basis differs but direction confirms. → Pricing pillar ↑
🔴 5%–10% rival cost advantage would shift DDR5/eSSD sourcing, once availability reaches parity (estimate); first read.
Demand: 🟢 Q3 demand 5%–10% above plan, HBM3E 5%–10% above, first read on demand vs plan; 2027 demand +20%–30% (estimate) vs SK hynix 2027 DRAM bit growth mid-20s% (SB #62470): consistent.

changes: Lead times: up to 20 weeks vs 14–16 weeks last quarter (expert's own comparison); first read in stored evidence, no earlier expert call.
DRAM pricing: about 30% y/y in Q3 (expert) vs SK hynix 3Q26 DRAM ASP +29% q/q (SB #67578): different basis, directionally confirming.
Allocation: slightly tighter q/q vs Meritz estimate of fulfilment falling from low-to-mid 80s% to ~80% in 2027 (SB #66240): confirming tightening.
New capacity: late 2027 into 2028 vs TrendForce meaningful capacity unlikely before 2028 (SB #63891): confirming.
